To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Lactate uptake by injured human brain is associated with increased lactate transport into brain and increased lactate production in brain.
lactate uptake into brain is associated with higher glucose uptake and that lactate is a major energy substrate for the injured human brain.

(1) lactate uptake into brain tissue was observed in the majority of patients with severe traumatic brain injury (2) lactate uptake was associated in time with higher arterial glucose levels (3) brain lactate concentrations were higher than arterial lactate concentrations in the majority of cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of lactate as an energy substrate by the injured brain.
understanding how the injured brain responds to trauma and how it adapts to the injury.
the brain's response to injury, and how the brain responds to injury by increasing its uptake of lactate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lactate uptake by the human brain after TBI is a physiological process, which occurs in parallel with lactate production.
lactate uptake is an energy sparing process for the injured brain.
lactate is an important substrate for the brain, and it is used by the brain in a similar manner to glucose, but with different kinetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

despite high brain lactate concentrations, lactate uptake into injured human brain is associated with high glucose uptake and is a potential mechanism to satisfy increased metabolic demands of the brain after TBJ.

lactate uptake into brain tissue is a physiological response to the brain's increased metabolic demand after traumatic brain injury, and is associated with a higher rate of glucose uptake into the brain.
lactate uptake is a mechanism to provide energy for the injured brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lactate is being used as an energy source by the brain in patients with traumatic brain injury (tBI), and this is occurring even when the brain is not hypoxic.
the injured brain is able to up-regulate the transport of lactate into the brain.
the injured human brain may use lactated as an alternative fuel.
